cards.title: Hierarchies and categories
cards.hook: Organise knowledge from broad to specific so properties flow down automatically.
cards.visual:
PrincipleMeaning
Inclusivenesstop class includes all subclasses
Species/differentiaonly one relation: is-a
Inheritancelower levels inherit higher-level properties
TransitivityA is-a B, B is-a C ⇒ A is-a C
Mutual exclusivitysiblings don't overlap
Necessary & sufficientmembership rules
Systematic & predictable rulessame rules to associate and distinguish
example: Recognise an animal as a cat → cat is a mammal → predict it bears live young, even if not yet observed.
cards.memory: I-S-I-T-M-N-S: Inclusive Species Inherit Transitively, Mutually exclusive, Necessary-sufficient, Systematic.
cards.trap: Hierarchies work best in MATURE domains with clear class boundaries.

cards.hook: Follow the links upward to inherit facts, unless a more specific exception overrides them.
formula: follow member/subclass links upward until a value is found
a more specific value takes precedence (Penguin cannot fly)
example: Tweety ∈ Canary ⊆ Bird ⊆ Animal → Tweety is an Animal, can fly, has wings.
Mary inherits Legs = 2 from Persons; John has an explicit Legs = 1.
cards.memory: Climb up for defaults, stop at the first answer.
cards.trap: The most SPECIFIC value wins, not the most general.

cards.title: Ontologies and knowledge graphs
cards.hook: An ontology defines exactly what concepts mean so a reasoner can derive and check facts.
cards.visual:
Ontology partExample
Classes & hierarchyStudent → subclass of → Person
PropertiesStudent → enrolledIn → Course; age 21
IndividualsMary → instance of → Student
AxiomsEvery Student is a Person
example: CB11.07 (a Room) enrols in Data Analytics → rejected (domain violated).
Data Analytics scheduledIn School of CS → inconsistent (range must be Room).
cards.memory: Semantic net = picture; ontology = picture + precise rules; knowledge graph = real facts.
cards.trap: A semantic network is intuitive and lightweight; an ONTOLOGY formally defines meaning for reliable reasoning.

cards.title: RDF and SPARQL
cards.hook: Ask a knowledge graph questions with triple patterns.
cards.visual:
LineMeaning
SELECT ?item ?itemLabel ?picvariables to return
?item wdt:P31 wd:Q146 .item is an instance of (P31) house cat (Q146)
?item wdt:P18 ?pic .item has an image (P18); items without one are excluded
SERVICE wikibase:label {…}adds readable labels like ?itemLabel
example: Douglas Adams (Q42) — instance of → Human; place of birth → Cambridge; author of → The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy.
cards.trap: wd: prefixes entities, wdt: prefixes direct-claim properties.
